style_context: Camping, cooking, tools, first aid, hiking, and fitness skills for the Tenderfoot rank

images.description: Photorealistic photo of an ordinary soft-sided backpack (no external frame, no hip belt) on a picnic table, viewed from a three-quarter angle, unzipped to show its main compartment: folded clothing (a t-shirt and socks) filling most of the visible space, with the top of a stuffed sleeping bag visible packed down low at the bottom near the back panel. A rolled sleeping pad is strapped to the outside top of the pack with external compression straps. A water bottle sits in an external mesh side pocket on the outside of the pack. A folded map peeks out of the top lid pocket. EXACTLY four callout labels total, each pointing to a different single item, and no other labels of any kind: 'Clothing' pointing to the folded clothes inside; 'Sleeping bag, packed low inside' pointing to the bag at the bottom; 'Sleeping pad, strapped outside' pointing to the rolled pad on the exterior; 'Water bottle, side pocket' pointing to the bottle in the mesh pocket. CRITICAL: each callout box contains its short label text exactly ONCE, on one or two lines — never repeat any word or line within the same callout box. Do not add any other callouts — no labels about straps, comfort, or any other feature.
images.value: Shows exactly where each category of gear belongs inside the pack, a spatial layout that a bulleted packing list cannot convey.

images.description: Clean educational diagram of three cooking pots arranged in a row on a picnic table or the ground, viewed from a slight angle, connected by simple left-to-right flow arrows: Pot 1 labeled 'Wash' showing soapy bubbles and a sponge; Pot 2 labeled 'Rinse' showing a plate half-submerged in plain clear water; Pot 3 labeled 'Sanitize' showing a single white sanitizing tablet being dropped into water. Exactly three pots, exactly three labels total, and nothing else — do NOT include a page title, heading, or banner of any kind above or around the pots.
images.value: Shows all three pots side by side with what belongs in each, a sequence that's easy to lose track of from a numbered list alone.

images.description: Photorealistic side-by-side photo comparison of a real two-person dome tent: left photo shows the rainfly sagging and touching the tent body at multiple points, labeled INCORRECT; right photo shows the same tent with the rainfly properly staked out with a clear air gap all around, labeled CORRECT. Real outdoor daytime campsite setting, no people.
images.value: Makes the rainfly contact problem, invisible in a written description, immediately visible side by side with the correct result.

images.description: Photorealistic overhead photo of a Scout in a clean field uniform crouched and whittling with a knife on the ground, with a dashed circle overlay drawn around them at arm's-length radius labeled 'clearance zone', and another person standing safely outside the circle.
images.value: Shows the actual size and shape of the safety clearance radius from a bird's-eye view, which a phrase like 'an arm's length' cannot convey spatially.

images.description: Photorealistic close-up photo of a hand drawing a knife blade across a whetstone during sharpening, with a small angle-indicator overlay showing the blade held at roughly 15-20 degrees from the stone's surface, and an arrow overlay showing the direction of the stroke. Hand and knife only, no face.
images.value: Shows the actual sharpening angle against the stone, a precise spatial relationship that a number like '15-20 degrees' is hard to picture without seeing it.

images.description: Photorealistic side-by-side photo comparison, side profile view: left photo shows a person's correct position for a nosebleed, head tilted forward, pinching the soft part of the nose, labeled CORRECT; right photo shows the incorrect position, head tilted back, labeled INCORRECT. Plain neutral background.
images.value: Makes the head-tilt direction, the one detail people get backward, immediately visible side by side with the wrong version.

images.description: Photorealistic side-by-side close-up photo comparison of a hand using fine-tipped tweezers on skin: left photo shows the correct technique, tweezers grasping close to the skin with a straight upward pull, labeled CORRECT; right photo shows the incorrect technique, a twisting motion, labeled INCORRECT. Close-up on hand and tweezers only, no face.
images.value: Makes the straight-pull versus twisting distinction visible at a glance, a fine hand-motion detail that written instructions are easy to misjudge.

images.description: Photorealistic macro close-up photo, framed as a tight torso-only crop: a pair of clasped fists positioned just above the navel of a shirt-covered stomach, forearms wrapping in from behind, in the Heimlich maneuver grip. The photograph shows ONLY a narrow horizontal band of the body from mid-chest to hips — no shoulders, no neck, no head, no face of either person anywhere in the frame, as if the camera were held at stomach height a few inches away. Two callout labels with arrows: one marking the fist placement, one marking the upward-and-inward thrust direction. No names, ages, or other demographic descriptors anywhere in the image; callout labels name only the technique.
images.value: Shows the exact fist position and thrust angle relative to the body that a written description like 'above the navel' leaves ambiguous.

images.description: Photorealistic three-panel close-up botanical photo comparison of real leaves on a plain neutral background: poison ivy's glossy three-leaflet cluster, poison oak's lobed three-leaflet cluster, and poison sumac's row of paired leaflets ending in a single leaflet. Each panel labeled with the plant name. Natural lighting, no people.
images.value: Lets a Scout compare the three plants' leaf shapes directly, since 'leaves of three' alone doesn't distinguish poison ivy from oak or explain why sumac looks different.

images.description: TRUE NADIR drone photo: camera pointing straight down at the ground with zero tilt, as if mounted on the belly of a drone hovering directly above — NOT an oblique or angled aerial view. The road must render as a perfectly straight vertical band running top to bottom with its two edges parallel to each other (no perspective convergence, no vanishing point, no visible horizon or tree canopy — this is a top-down plan view, not a 3/4 aerial shot). The road has a paved travel lane with a painted white edge line, and beyond that edge line, a gravel or dirt shoulder bordered by grass. A line of Scouts in bright or reflective vests walks in strict single file on the unpaved gravel/dirt shoulder, entirely OUTSIDE and to the left of the white edge line — none of them are on the paved travel lane. A car occupies the paved lane, positioned ahead of the line of Scouts. The gap between the Scouts (on the shoulder) and the car (on the pavement) must be clearly visible.
images.value: Shows the correct positioning relative to the road and oncoming traffic from above, a spatial layout hard to picture from a text rule alone.

images.description: Photorealistic side-view photo of a Scout seated on the ground in the back-saver sit-and-reach test position: one leg extended straight forward, the other leg bent with the foot flat, reaching forward with both hands toward the extended foot, back straight.
images.value: Shows the correct seated leg and reach position for the test, a body posture that's easy to get wrong without seeing it.

images.description: Photorealistic photo of a real American flag displayed flat against a wall, viewed from the observer's perspective, with the blue star field (the union) correctly positioned in the upper left corner from the viewer's point of view, and a small label overlay marking 'observer's left'.
images.value: Shows exactly which corner the union belongs in from the viewer's perspective, a spatial rule that's easy to flip backward without seeing it.
